g.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS: ECMWF's forecast via Open-Meteo. CAMS: satellite irradiance service. Dot: estimate at the main XGBoost tuning setting. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Every lead day is scored on the same farm-hours, those that all six lead days hold. The intervals of two rows overlap more than the paired differences between rows would. Rows run in ladder order, not best first. A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar. F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective energy (CAPE), convective inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface temperature, snow, precipitation, pressure, wind, gusts. IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day. FP: F0 plus dew point, pressure, precipitation, and wind speed, the variables the production forecast already receives. Lead day L: the forecast was issued L days before the day it describes, so lead day 1 is the morning before. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.'

text.font-family: Matter XH, DM Sans, sans-serif
text.tspan: Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS: ECMWF's forecast via Open-Meteo. CAMS:
Dot: estimate at the main XGBoost tuning setting. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months.
Every lead day is scored on the same farm-hours, those that all six lead days hold. The intervals of two rows
overlap more than the paired differences between rows would. Rows run in ladder order, not best first.
A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar.
F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and
high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective
energy (CAPE), convective inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface temperature, snow,
IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day.
FP: F0 plus dew point, pressure, precipitation, and wind speed, the variables the production forecast already
Lead day L: the forecast was issued L days before the day it describes, so lead day 1 is the morning before.
Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
